correctness.rationale: The composition table defines an acyclic category since there are no triples of composable nonidentity arrows. The three diagonal long edges are free faces and delete exactly their own triangles. The retained edges are all double-incidence, and each link is a single six-cycle (the a,b; a,c; and b,c incidence graphs). Around the six row/column adjacencies the signs of t_02 and t_21 agree, but their shared c_1 edge requires opposite signs. The collapsed complex is therefore a connected closed nonorientable surface with 3-9+6=0, hence the Klein bottle. Two-object acyclic nerves are graphs and cannot have its order-two H₁ torsion. This is a direct proof from RESULT.md lines 8–28; checker.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. The original nerve is only homotopy equivalent to the bottle; arrow-count minimality is not claimed.

evidence: The universal theorem gives ν=3 for every connected finite at-most-two-dimensional CW homotopy type other than contractible and graph types. The Klein bottle meets all hypotheses and torsion rules out both exceptions. Carcacía-Campos separately proves the torsion lower bound; his Proposition 2.4 only concerns two first-stage arrows, so that particular classification alone does not give the present upper bound.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Substituting the Klein bottle in the universal theorem gives the exact invariant with no additional existence proof. The same-day date is not used to order the records.

evidence: Label the three vertex colors 0,1,2. Every core triangle uniquely specifies a pair of edges 01 and 12 because repeated pairs would give a forbidden dual two-cycle. Each use of a short edge accounts for two triangles, so the missing cells form a perfect matching; relabel to put it on the diagonal. Give each missing composite a distinct private 02 edge.

evidence: Section 8 cites the classical crystallization encoding a closed PL n-manifold by a pseudo-triangulation with n+1 vertices. In dimension two the contracted colored complex has one vertex of each color. For the Klein bottle Euler characteristic and double incidence force six triangles and nine edges.

The dual is properly three-edge-colored by the omitted vertex color. For any two chosen colors the subgraph is a six-cycle because it follows the link at the corresponding primal vertex. Thus no pair of triangles can share two edges: that would form a separate two-cycle. The dual is a simple cubic graph on six vertices and nonbipartite by surface nonorientability.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A simple cubic graph on six vertices is the triangular prism or K_{3,3}, by taking its 2-regular complement; nonbipartiteness forces the prism. Its edge coloring is unique up to relabeling: the colors around one triangular face force the three spoke colors, then force the colors on the other face. The frozen off-diagonal table has this colored prism dual (the c-pairs close the two triangles). Thus the explicit retained surface is precisely the elementary crystallization core, not just an unrelated three-vertex complex.

As a research finding, however, the exact object invariant is already a special case of the universal theorem, and the compact collapse model is the classical six-triangle crystallization with missing composites filled by private edges. The record proves no minimum arrow count, uniqueness or different structural result that would give the model independent research value. No repair is offered.
